catalog_quote: Stress is realised as a slightly louder and lengthened syllable. Stress assignment is partly fixed and partly Iexically assigned. Most words have stress on their initial syllable. A very small proportion of words (something around 0.05% in the corpus) has stress on their second syllable. Of these, many are old reduplications ...; that is, the word looks as if its first CV syllable has been reduplicated. Others are obvious recent loan words which retain the stress pattern of the original word. For the rest, there is no obvious formal reason for the non -initial stress. It appears simply to be a property of these words. A very few words have stress on their third syllable. ... Most words have stress on the initial syllable. In particular almost all CVCV words (including all CVCV nouns) are stressed on the initial syllable. ... Many two-syllable words of the form CVCVC have stress on the s…
